wormald.wormald_heading: 8 (iv) Oxford, Bodleian Library, Vet. A.3 c.196
wormald.shelfmark: Oxford, Bodleian Library, Vet. A.3 c.196 (Whelock's edition of Lambarde's Archaionomia, annotated by Richard Taylor, 1811), witness to a lost parchment leaf once owned by Mr Stevenson of Norwich
wormald.wormald_date: Taylor's notes and facsimile 1811 (Table 4.1); the lost Norwich leaf s. xii (Ker), late-12th-century (Sisam), p. 260
wormald.wormald_origin: The lost leaf was pasted inside the cover of a later manuscript owned by Mr Stevenson, printer, of Norwich; Richard Taylor, owner of the MS in 1811, saw it, entered its variants in the margins (pp. 62–4) of his Lambarde/Whelock and apparently made the facsimile now attached inside the back cover. The MS later belonged to Kenneth Sisam, whose daughter Celia Sisam gave it to the Bodleian (p. 259 and n. 367).
wormald.laws: II–III Eg (the leaf's text breaks off; 52 lines in Taylor's facsimile)
wormald.other_contents: Printed Archaionomia (Whelock) with Taylor's marginal variants, signed and dated note (foot of p. 62), facsimile of the leaf, and a translation begun and abandoned on the facsimile's first facing verso.
wormald.overview: A copy in the Bodleian of Lambarde's Archaionomia, as reissued by Whelock, in which Richard Taylor entered, in 1811, the readings of a now-lost twelfth-century parchment leaf of II–III Edgar that he had seen at Norwich, apparently adding a careful facsimile of it. The leaf seems to have been a plain copy in long lines, probably not from a luxury MS, perhaps from one of the twelfth-century legal compilations or a stand-alone copy like Harley 55(B). Its text, like those of Nero A.i(A) and Quadripartitus, lacks the variants of the Wulfstan manuscripts, and it is further evidence both of interest in Old English law under Henry II and of the circulation of the major codes in differing versions.
wormald.key_quote: 'Here, in any case, is a further sign that interest in Anglo-Saxon vernacular legislation was still alive into Henry II's time' (p. 260)
wormald.doubts: Not in the guide and unknown to Liebermann (Sisam announced it in 1953). Ker, Catalogue no. 411; variants in Whitelock, Councils and Synods, pp. 95–102. Wormald spells 'Whelock' (guide 'Wheloc'). Text includes 'eft' in the unjust-reeve clause, as Nero A.i(A) (p. 260). Consider adding as a new guide entry.
verify_notes: shelfmark: removed '1644', not given by Wormald.

Taylor's making of the facsimile is Wormald's inference ('seems ... though he does not say so', p. 259): softened in origin and overview; 'about twenty-six lines to the page' reworded, as Wormald only envisages 26 long lines from 52 in all.
pages: Table 4.1 entry is on p. 165 only.
overview: reworded to remove five-word runs shared with Wormald.
